stimulus.source_note: Paraphrase of Barron's Premium 2027, Chapter 10, Topic 8.4, Levittown and Suburban Development.
stimulus.text: After the war, builder William Levitt bought farmland outside New York City and built Levittown, a development of thousands of nearly identical, modest houses put up quickly with mass-production methods. The houses were cheap enough for many returning veterans to buy with GI Bill loans. Levitt barred African American buyers with restrictive covenants, and Federal Housing Administration rules encouraged builders to sell only to white buyers. Songwriter Malvina Reynolds mocked the sameness of such developments in 'Little Boxes' (1962).

stem: Levitt built Levittown houses quickly and cheaply by using which method?

options.text: Handcrafted houses built one at a time by local carpenters
options.misconception: Background from the books: Levitt applied mass-production methods, the opposite of one-at-a-time handcrafting.

options.text: Houses shipped whole from factories in Europe
options.misconception: Background from the books: Levitt built the houses on farmland outside New York City; they were not shipped from Europe.

options.text: Houses paid for entirely by the federal government
options.misconception: Background from the books: veterans bought the houses with GI Bill loans; the government did not pay for them outright.

options.text: Mass-production methods that turned out many nearly identical houses

rationales.A: Background from the books: Levitt used mass-production methods, the opposite of building one house at a time by hand.
rationales.B: Background from the books: the houses were built on farmland outside New York City, not shipped whole from Europe.
rationales.C: Background from the books: veterans bought the houses with GI Bill loans; the government backed the loans but did not buy the houses.
rationales.D: The passage says Levitt applied mass production to houses, building them rapidly and cheaply in huge developments.
rationales.general:
1. Look for the building method in the passage: farmland, thousands of houses, mass production.
2. Mass production means many nearly identical products made quickly and cheaply, which matches Levittown exactly.
3. Handcrafting, shipping houses from Europe, and full federal payment all contradict what the passage says about how Levitt built.
Remember: When a passage names a method, the answer repeats that method in plain words.
